brief.headline: Move from 100% advance payment to normal 30-day credit and match the ₹66.48/KG we already pay Sayaji

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹66.48/KG — the price Sayaji Industries already gives us for the same Dextrose
priceAsk.basis: We're paying them ₹70.80/KG, which is 6.5% more than Sayaji's ₹66.48/KG. The open market shows Dextrose Anhydrous IP typically trades at ₹66–73/kg, so our target sits right in that band. No reason to pay above what we already get elsewhere.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Switch from paying 100% in advance to standard 30-day credit after delivery
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash that's currently locked in advance payments

brief.financialLeverage: They're a ₹1555.82 Cr company keeping 2.9% of every sale as profit, so margins are tight — but they're growing sales fast at 29.7% per year, which means they want new orders. We're tiny to them: our ₹1.06 Cr is just 0.07% of their revenue, so on our own we have almost no pull. Their overall health scores only D (44/100), meaning moderate risk. The play is to dangle a multi-year commitment or more volume in exchange for the price match and payment switch, and to quietly line up Gulshan or Sanstar as a second source so they know we can walk.

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: ₹2437.35 Cr listed maker, health B (68/100) — established dextrose supplier and a drop-in alternate; strongest backup to qualify

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: ₹842.97 Cr recently-listed maize specialist, health C (52/100) — growing capacity in dextrose; second choice to RFQ

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: ₹365.39 Cr Indore wet-miller making Dextrose ANHYDROUS IV-fluid grade (exact form match); health D (27/100) so verify stability, but a credible local alternate

risks: We're only 0.07% of their business, so they may ignore us unless we bundle more volume or a longer contract to make it worth their while.

Their 2.9% profit margin is paper-thin — push the payment switch hard (it costs them nothing), but go gently on price so we don't destabilise supply; frame the price ask as matching what they see in the market, not a hard cut.
Their D (44/100) health score flags moderate risk — don't put all our eggs here; get Gulshan or Sanstar qualified and priced in parallel so we have a live second source before the next renewal.
We're paying 100% advance today, which is extreme — they'll resist losing that cash cushion, so offer to phase in (say 50% advance, 50% at 15 days first) or sweeten it with a volume commitment.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move you onto normal 30-day terms and bring your Dextrose price to ₹66.48 — the rate Sayaji already gives us and right in line with the market — and in return we're ready to talk about a longer commitment or more volume.
